Braised Chicken Legs with Rice, Potatoes & Veggies🍗 Ingredients * 1 package chicken drumsticks (6–7 pieces) * 1-2 tbsp olive oil * 1 tsp salt * 1 tsp black pepper * 2 tsp garlic powder * 2 tsp onion powder * 2 tsp paprika * ½ tsp cumin * 1 jalapeño, diced * ½ red onion, diced * 1 tbsp sun-dried tomato paste * 1 tbsp @Loisa sofrito * 5–6 garlic cloves, minced * 4 cups chicken stock * 1 (8 oz) can tomato sauce * Small potatoes, halved (about 10–12 baby potatoes) * 1 zucchini, diced * Cooked white rice, for serving (let me know if you guys want my rice recipe) Instructions: 1. Clean the chicken with vinegar, then pat completely dry with paper towels. 2. Season the chicken with the salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and cumin. Toss until evenly coated. 3. Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or deep skillet over medium-high heat. 4. Brown the chicken for 2–3 minutes per side until golden. It doesn’t need to be cooked through. Remove and set aside. 5. In the same pot, add the diced jalapeño and red onion. Cook for about 5 minutes until softened. 6. Stir in the sun-dried tomato paste and cook for 30 seconds. 7. Add the Loisa Sofrito and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. 8. Pour in the chicken stock and tomato sauce, stirring to combine. Bring to a gentle boil. 9. Return the chicken to the pot. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for about 1 hour, or until the chicken is fall-apart tender and the sauce has reduced. 10. About 20 minutes before the chicken is done, add the halved potatoes and diced zucchini. Continue simmering until the potatoes are fork-tender and the zucchini is cooked. 11. Serve over fluffy white rice and spoon plenty of the sauce over the top. #chickenlegs #braised #onepotmeals #cookwithme

Another fun training day with my daughter, Lucy! Lucy woke up and asked if I could run her through a workout so of course we hit it.  As a 9 year old, we do a vast mix of training, but this training can be applied to any age (with modifications, of course): Cone game - lateral movement focus. This is a game the kids love and it’s a great warm up. Stand there and throw some cones back and forth while they try to “knock as many as they can” down. They don’t realize the reaction and lateral movement they are creating by simply playing a game!  Sandbag drags (or sled drag) is great for any age. Great from the ground up. If you suffer from knee pain, I highly suggest reverse sledding or reverse treadmill.  Dead hangs.  Amazing for grip strength, spinal decompression, shoulder mobility, back, core. Studies show grip strength is one of the strongest indicators of longevity.  Pushups. Lucy is killing it on the elevated pushups. This set she hit 13 with good form. We have moved her down every week and pretty soon she will be killing them from the floor.  Jumping. By far the best thing for children imo. Requires power and strength, coordination, and deceleration. Power is lost way before strength in adults. Somewhere along the lines adults stop jumping and creating true power and it’s a detriment to our capabilities.  Isometrics. Awesome for any age. Great for joint-angle specificity and muscle growth.  These workouts are not just for my 9 year old. Modifications can be made for any fitness level. Get out there and get after it today! Have you ever craved something you’ve never even had before? 😂 I randomly thought, what if I turned potatoes into boba? And let me tell you… they’re SO chewy and delicious!  Potato Boba Ingredients 3–4 russet potatoes 1 cup potato starch Salt, to taste For the chili oil topping 1 tsp gochugaru 1 tbsp chopped parsley or green onions 1 tbsp minced garlic 1 tbsp soy sauce 2–3 tbsp hot oil 1. Steam or boil the potatoes until fork tender (I steamed mine). 2. Mash them while they’re still hot. Add the potato starch and salt, then knead into a smooth dough. If it’s too dry, add a little water. 3. Roll the dough into small boba-sized balls. 4. Boil until they float to the surface, then transfer them to cold water. Drain well. 5. Place the potato boba in a bowl. Add the gochugaru, parsley or green onions, garlic, and soy sauce. 6. Pour the hot oil over everything and mix until well coated.
